en: Points of Controversy Great Chapter Fifteen Eighteenth Section
The Discourse on the Single Path:
One realizes the four fruits of recluseship by means of a single noble path? Yes.
Is there a convergence of four types of contact …pe… of four types of perception?
One should not say so …pe…
Does one realize the four fruits of recluseship by means of a single noble path?
Yes. Is it by means of the stream-entry path? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … by means of the path of the once-returner … [as before] … or the path of the non-returner?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … By which path?
By the path of arahantship.
Does one abandon personality-belief, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances by means of the path of arahantship?
One should not say so … [as before] … Does one abandon personality-belief,
doubt, and adherence to rules and observances by means of the path of arahantship?
“Yes.
“But has it not been stated by the Blessed One that the fruit of stream-entry is the abandoning of the three fetters?
“Yes.”
If the abandoning of the three fetters is stated by the Blessed One to be the fruit of stream-entry, then surely it should not be said:
"By the path of arahantship, one abandons personality-belief, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances.
Is it not the case that by the path of arahantship, one abandons gross sensual lust and gross ill-will?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does one abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will by means of the path of arahantship? Yes.
Is it not said by the Blessed One that the fruit of the once-returner is the attenuation of sensual lust and ill will? Yes.

If it is indeed said by the Blessed One that the fruit of the once-returner is the attenuation of sensual lust and ill will, then surely you should not say [that this is the fruit of the non-returner].
“It is by the path of arahantship that one abandons gross sensual lust and gross ill will.
[If you say this,] must you not also say: “It is by the path of arahantship that one abandons subtle sensual lust and subtle ill will”?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is it not the case that one abandons even the subtlest residual attachment to sensual desire and even the subtlest residual ill will by means of the path of arahantship?
Yes, it is.
But has it not been stated by the Blessed One that the abandonment of sensual desire and ill will without remainder constitutes the fruit of non-returning?
“Yes.
“If the Blessed One has stated that the fruit of non-returning is the abandonment of sensual lust and ill will without remainder, then surely it should not be said:
‘By the path of arahantship, one abandons the residual trace of sensual lust and the residual trace of ill will.’”
Is it not to be said that one realizes the four fruits of recluseship by means of a single noble path?
Yes, it is.
"Was the path of stream-entry developed by the Blessed One?
"Yes.
"Is the Blessed One a stream-enterer?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Has the path of the once-returner … [and] the path of the non-returner been developed by the Blessed One?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the Blessed One a non-returner?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
The Blessed One realizes the four fruits of recluseship by means of a single noble path; his disciples realize the four fruits of recluseship by means of the four noble paths?
Yes. Do the disciples of the Buddha, the Blessed One, see what has not been seen, attain what has not been attained, and realize what has not been realized? [Yes.]
It should not be stated thus... [etc.
...The Discussion on the Single Path is finished.
